title: No Measurable Benefit from Verifier‑Assisted Generate→Validate→Repair under Shared‑Initial Generation: A Preregistered Emulation Study
abstract: We preregistered and autonomously executed a paired emulation study (study-cnd-2026-001) that tested whether a verifier‑assisted generate→validate→repair pipeline improves oracle pass rates for LLM‑produced network configurations on vendor‑diverse emulated NetOps intent→configuration tasks. Key frozen design choices: paired design (Npairs=200), generation semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one shared generated candidate per pair consumed by both conditions), model = gpt-5-mini (declared), validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (deterministic emulator), and repair budget ≤1 call/task. Execution completed as preregistered (planned_episode_count=400; completed_episode_count=400; model_calls_used=200). Both baseline and guarded conditions produced oracle‑passing configurations for all 200 pairs (baseline 200/200, guarded 200/200). Absolute paired difference = 0.00 (paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.00,0.00]; McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00). Critically, because the preregistered generation semantics produced a single shared candidate per pair that passed the deterministic oracle in every case, the guarded repair stage was never invoked (repair calls invoked = 0). We release the full artifact bundle (preregistration, prompts, raw outputs, provider traces, validator traces, execution manifest and per‑file SHA‑256 hashes) and interpret this null confirmatory outcome as a design‑bound result that highlights how generation semantics, task difficulty, oracle coverage, and repair budget determine whether verifier‑assisted pipelines can show measurable benefit.

sections.introduction: Automated intent→configuration translation is a high‑value NetOps use case for generative LLMs but suffers known failure modes (hallucination, vendor‑idiom mismatch, unsafe ordering). Verifier‑assisted generate→validate→repair workflows are a promising mitigation: generation proposes candidate configs, deterministic validators check objective properties, and repair modules iteratively fix violations. We preregistered a confirmatory paired experiment to quantify whether a verifier‑assisted pipeline increases oracle pass rate relative to unconstrained generation. Research question (preregistered): under the frozen experimental plan, does a verifier‑assisted generate→validate→repair pipeline increase the oracle pass rate (primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline)? Contributions: (1) an artifact‑backed preregistered paired emulation study with full auditing artifacts; (2) a reproducible report that the preregistered design produced a design‑bound null result (no measurable benefit) together with the deterministic accounting that explains why; (3) methodological recommendations for future guarded‑pipeline evaluations. The reader should note: the null confirmatory outcome is bounded to the exact preregistered design and generation semantics (see Methods and Disclosure).
sections.related_work: Recent work studies LLMs for network configuration and reliability aids. Prior evaluations of intent→configuration mapping and NetOps LLMs include NetConfEval and additional intent‑to‑config prototypes that measure translation fidelity and highlight vendor‑idiom errors [Chang et al.; Wang et al.]. Constraint‑and‑validator approaches (e.g., MeshAgent) have shown practical gains using explicit invariants and abstention mechanisms [Zhou et al.]. Verifier‑grounded repair workflows in other domains (StruSpec) demonstrate that verifier‑produced counterexamples can materially improve repair success. Our study differs by preregistering a deterministic paired protocol, freezing generation semantics, and publishing an auditable execution manifest so that a null effect can be traced to explicit, archived design choices (see cited artifact list).
sections.methodology: Preregistration and frozen design: The study preregistration (study-cnd-2026-001; preregistration SHA‑256 = a8969ac01f3b1bb7585872c58a92f72d0752160dd4e6e01cbafbfe0d15073ad2) fixed the confirmatory hypothesis, sampling, estimand, generation semantics, model, validator, repair budget, stopping rules, and analysis. Design summary (frozen): paired binary design with Npairs=200 (each pair = same task under two conditions: baseline (unconstrained) vs guarded (verifier‑assisted)). Protocol buckets and vendor stratification were preregistered (BGP/OSPF/ACL/VLAN and Cisco/Juniper/Arista) and appear in the archived task manifest. Model and adapter: declared model = gpt-5-mini via the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter; model configuration artifact archived at execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). Validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (deterministic emulation oracle) scored every candidate; scoring traces are archived (execution/scoring/; representative file SHA‑256s given below). Crucial preregistered generation semantics: shared_initial_candidate, i.e., one candidate was generated per pair and consumed by both the baseline and guarded conditions (this choice was preregistered and is authoritative; see preregistration SHA‑256 above). Repair policy: at most one repair call per task; repairs only invoked when validation fails. Execution logging: every provider call, raw response, and validator trace was recorded and hashed; the execution manifest lists per‑file SHA‑256 digests and execution accounting (see execution/execution_manifest.json in the artifacts). Analysis plan: primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline analyzed with paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) and exact McNemar two‑sided test; primary missingness policy = complete pairs only (pairs with provider/infrastructure failures would be excluded and logged).
sections.results: Execution accounting and deterministic reconciliation: execution completed as preregistered: planned_episode_count=400, completed_episode_count=400, failed_episode_count=0, model_calls_used=200 (one shared generation per pair). Deterministic reconciliation artifacts confirm accounting consistency (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json, SHA‑256 = 799b23b993fcc9c04fc4d0a375e975937bc11d9f8c6595d43dce94375411d174). Confirmatory outcome (artifact‑backed): complete_pairs = 200; baseline_successes = 200/200 (rate 1.0); guarded_successes = 200/200 (rate 1.0); absolute paired difference = 0.00; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00] (bootstrap_resamples = 10,000; seed = 1729); McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00. Relevant artifacts: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 = 7bc1bd2a42b5ac3f7adb61db47cf8dbe0472f678032abcd1e7c44f92ea2de71c) and analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA‑256 = 1cb072b4db7c8e29212ef28b97baccb66a507a7c8b8ceaad35b7e84f7976a951) contain the numeric contingency and summary reported above. Repair activity: repair calls invoked = 0; repair_applied_count = 0. Representative scoring traces (validator outputs) for a canonical pair are archived (execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json; SHA‑256 = eaf96aec12c30860a6fd70987289cc71104134a3330b99c7e024f244dbd35c1b). The shared candidate responsible for the unanimous pass is archived (execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt; SHA‑256 = f8de4d6e1a625e42ba4907440b4377c78949ed56446e5c73030bc267e56abfaf).
sections.discussion: Interpretation and design‑bound null: The preregistered null confirmatory result is definitive for the exact frozen design: because generation semantics were shared_initial_candidate and every shared candidate passed the deterministic oracle, the guarded repair stage was never invoked and therefore could not improve oracle pass rates. This is a design‑bound null result—it does not imply verifier‑assisted architectures are ineffective in general. The outcome highlights three experimental axes that govern whether guarded pipelines can show measurable benefit: (A) generation independence: shared vs independent sampling controls whether the guarded condition sees a different candidate set than baseline; (B) task difficulty and oracle coverage: easy tasks or high oracle coverage create ceiling effects; (C) repair budget and iteration policy: limited repair budget (≤1 call/task, preregistered) constrains how much correction can occur. For future evaluations we recommend (i) explicitly preregister generation semantics (shared vs independent); (ii) pre‑assess oracle coverage and design task difficulty to avoid baseline ceiling effects; (iii) allocate repair budget and iteration rules appropriate to anticipated failure rates. All artifacts needed to reproduce or to re‑run an independent‑generation variant are released in the bundle (see execution manifest and per‑file hashes).
sections.conclusion: Under the preregistered, artifact‑backed design (shared_initial_candidate semantics, gpt-5-mini, deterministic_netops_validator_v5, Npairs=200), both baseline and guarded conditions passed the oracle for every pair and the guarded repair stage was never invoked. The resulting confirmatory estimate is an absolute paired difference of 0.00 (95% bootstrap CI [0.00,0.00]; McNemar p = 1.00). This design‑bound null result underscores that generation semantics and task/oracle difficulty must be chosen to allow repairs to be exercised when evaluating verifier‑assisted pipelines. We publish the full artifact bundle so researchers can (a) re-run independent‑generation variants, (b) increase task difficulty or repair budget, and (c) more precisely measure where verifier‑assistance yields measurable operational benefit. All artifacts, per‑file SHA‑256 digests, and the preregistration are archived and referenced below for reproducibility.

disclosure_statement:
Mandatory Disclosure Statement (artifact‑backed):
- Initial master prompt reference (immutable archive): provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). This master prompt launched the autonomous post‑lock research run. The Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and constrained the master prompt before the autonomy lock; all other substantive research steps described in this paper were performed autonomously after the autonomy lock.
- Preregistration: study id = study-cnd-2026-001; preregistration SHA‑256 = a8969ac01f3b1bb7585872c58a92f72d0752160dd4e6e01cbafbfe0d15073ad2. The preregistration froze hypotheses, sampling, stopping rules, generation semantics (shared_initial_candidate), repair budget (≤1 repair call/task), estimand, and analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1 with paired bootstrap 10,000 resamples, seed=1729).
- Models and adapter: declared model = gpt-5-mini used via the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter family; model configuration artifact: execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). Provider call traces and raw responses for every model invocation are archived under execution/provider_calls/ and execution/responses/ with per‑file SHA‑256 digests recorded in the execution manifest.
- Generation semantics (frozen): shared_initial_candidate (one candidate generated per pair and consumed by both conditions). This preregistered choice is central to the observed outcome: model_calls_used = 200 (one shared generation per 200 pairs) and therefore the guarded repair stage had no opportunity to operate because the shared candidates passed the deterministic oracle in every pair (repair calls invoked = 0). The execution manifest records these counts and per‑file hashes (see execution/execution_manifest.json in the artifact bundle).
- Validator and oracle: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (deterministic emulation oracle) scored every candidate. Representative scoring artifacts: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (SHA‑256 = eaf96aec12c30860a6fd70987289cc71104134a3330b99c7e024f244dbd35c1b). All validator traces are archived and hashed.
- Repair policy and budgeting: preregistered maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; in this run repair calls invoked = 0 and repair_applied_count = 0 (artifact-backed). All repair prompts, if used, would have been archived; none were required.
- Analysis executor and settings (frozen): paired_binary_analysis_v1, paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) and exact McNemar two‑sided test. Confirmatory artifacts: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 = 7bc1bd2a42b5ac3f7adb61db47cf8dbe0472f678032abcd1e7c44f92ea2de71c) and analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA‑256 = 1cb072b4db7c8e29212ef28b97baccb66a507a7c8b8ceaad35b7e84f7976a951).
- Execution and reproducibility procedures: all prompts, model outputs, provider traces, validator traces, scoring files, manifests, and analysis artifacts were immutably recorded and their SHA‑256 hashes are listed in the execution manifest. Deterministic reconciliation confirms accounting consistency (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json; SHA‑256 = 799b23b993fcc9c04fc4d0a375e975937bc11d9f8c6595d43dce94375411d174).
- Human involvement: the Research Director provided the initial topic family selection and approved the master prompt before the autonomy lock and engaged in pre‑lock instrumentation and rehearsal. After the autonomy lock, all literature review, question selection, preregistration, experiment design, code generation, execution, analysis, and manuscript drafting were performed autonomously by the system. No human performed manual substantive editing of the manuscript after the autonomy lock. Pre‑lock development artifacts were not used as final‑study evidence unless reproduced under the frozen post‑lock workflow.
- Deviations and failures: none relevant to the primary confirmatory analysis; no provider/model‑identifier drift occurred; no pairs were excluded; repair stage was not triggered (repair calls invoked = 0). The full execution manifest and per‑file hashes are included in the released artifact bundle for audit and reproduction.
limitations: Confirmatory scope limited to the exact preregistered design (shared_initial_candidate semantics, single model gpt-5-mini, deterministic_netops_validator_v5, synthetic task bank of 200); results do not generalize beyond these frozen choices.

Shared_initial_candidate execution semantics eliminated independent sampling variance between baseline and guarded conditions and therefore prevented the guarded pipeline from exercising repairs in this run; this design choice was preregistered and materially caused the observed null effect.
Synthetic emulated tasks and a deterministic emulator‑based oracle do not fully represent production heterogeneity (real devices, vendor image idiosyncrasies, transient runtime faults).
Single‑model experiment limits generality across LLM families, instruction tuning, and deployment‑specific behaviors.
Repair budget was restricted to one repair call per preregistration; richer iterative repair policies remain unexplored in this run.
Oracle blind spots (coverage gaps) remain possible; oracle‑coverage diagnostics are included in the artifact bundle and flagged where applicable.
